stories.title: Add the CPU reference X-ray image (renderDrrCpu) with the absorption law
stories.description: Create src/render/pipeline.ts and src/render/drrCpu.ts. pipeline.ts holds the numbers both renderers share (move MARCH_STEP_MM and ABSORPTION_PER_MM there from drrGpu.ts and import them back; no behaviour change on the GPU) and, in a comment at the top, the ORDER OF STEPS every later story follows. Taking the image (frozen until the next exposure): (1) magnification m: image pixel p uses the detector position centre + (p − centre) / m, centre = (256, 256); (2) ray from the source through that detector position, total absorption = sum over 0.5 mm steps of (intensity/255 × ABSORPTION_PER_MM + extra/255 × EXTRA_ABSORPTION_PER_MM) × step, value = e^(−total); (3) noise (seeded grain) added, result kept within 0…1; (4) collimation: pixels outside the open area get the fixed 'no signal' value and no noise. Displaying the held image (applied straight away, no new exposure): (5) invert: value → 1 − value; (6) flip left-right, flip up-down, then rotate clockwise by 0/90/180/270°. This story builds step 2 without the extra volume. renderDrrCpu(volume, pose, options) returns { width: 512, height: 512, data: Float32Array } with values 0…1 (1 = full brightness), pixel (x, y) at index x + 512 × y, y counted from the top; each pixel's ray comes from createProjection(pose).unproject at the pixel centre (x + 0.5, y + 0.5). Use the same sampling as the GPU shader (nearest voxel, samples at entry + (i + 0.5) × step inside the volume's box). Also export a one-pixel function (e.g. transmissionAt(volume, projection, pixel, options)) so unit tests can check single rays quickly. Volumes are always in the standard layout (identity orientation; owner decision 2026-11-10: the F1 converter standardises files), so throw a clear error for any other orientation. Voxel spacing may differ per axis. Plain TypeScript, no browser code.
acceptance: Unit test: for an empty volume (all intensity 0) every one of the 512×512 values is exactly 1
Unit test: for a uniform slab across the beam at pose (0°, 0°), the centre pixel's value goes down each time the slab gets thicker (at least three thicknesses)
Unit test: doubling the slab thickness squares the transmitted fraction at the centre pixel, within 2%
Unit test: a volume whose orientation is not the identity is rejected with a clear error
Unit test: on the phantom at the default pose, the pixel at the projected centre of the upper vertebra block is darker than the pixel at (0, 0)
The existing render screen tests still pass (the GPU image is unchanged)
stories.verify: npx vitest run tests/render/drrCpu.test.ts && npx playwright test tests/e2e/render

stories.title: Add the render settings (invert, magnification, collimation, noise level, flips, rotation) and report them in window.__sim
stories.description: Create src/render/settings.ts: the RenderSettings type { invert: boolean; magnification: 1 | 1.5 | 2; collimation: { left, right, top, bottom } (each the percentage of the field covered from that edge, 0–50); noiseLevel (0–1); flipHorizontal: boolean; flipVertical: boolean; rotation: 0 | 90 | 180 | 270 }, the defaults (not inverted, 1×, shutters fully open, noiseLevel 0 for now, no flips, rotation 0), a function that validates a change (numbers outside their range are clamped; non-finite numbers and values that are not one of the allowed options are ignored), and a small zone-local settings store (get, set, subscribe) with one shared instance. The settings have NO effect on the image yet; later stories switch them on one by one. In fluoroCanvas.ts, remember for each exposure the pose, a copy of the settings and the image's noise seed (an image counter: 1 for the first image after page load, then 2, 3 …). Register a read-only getter with registerDebugGetter('render', …) so window.__sim.render() returns { settings, lastImage } where lastImage is null before the first image and otherwise { pose, settings, noiseSeed }. Add the zone's screen-test helper tests/e2e/render/renderPage.ts (not a spec file): setRenderSettings(page, patch) changes the settings through the app's own settings module as served by the dev server (the same trick as setPose in tests/fixtures/simPage.ts), and getRenderInfo(page) returns window.__sim.render(). No edits in src/core/ or tests/fixtures/.

stories.title: Draw the image in two steps (take, then display) and add Invert to both renderers
stories.description: Change the GPU drawing to two steps, following the order of steps documented at the top of src/render/pipeline.ts: on each exposure the X-ray image is rendered into an off-screen image (a WebGLRenderTarget) and kept; a second, cheap display step draws that held image to the canvas. The display step is re-run whenever a display setting (invert now; flips and rotation later) changes, WITHOUT a new exposure — so the learner sees Invert immediately and the shot count does not change (owner decision 2026-11-10). Because the held image is reused, nothing else on screen may change when Invert is toggled (this protects last image hold, F3.5 and F7.4). Add invert to the display step (value → 1 − value) and to renderDrrCpu as options.invert. No on-screen button yet (next story): tests switch it with setRenderSettings.

stories.title: Add seeded X-ray grain (noise) to the CPU reference, with default levels for shots and fluoro
stories.description: Create src/render/noise.ts and add options.noise { seed, level } to renderDrrCpu as step 3 of the order of steps documented at the top of src/render/pipeline.ts: a zero-mean random amount, the same every time for the same seed and pixel, scaled by the level (0 = none, 1 = maximum) and added to the value, which is then kept within 0…1. Collimated pixels get no noise. Put two default levels in pipeline.ts, DEFAULT_NOISE_LEVEL = { shot, fluoro } with fluoro higher than shot and shot above 0, and export defaultNoiseLevel(kind: 'shot' | 'fluoro').
